Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly‑rated and widely‑praised crime‑thriller films released in 2020. These picks span a range of styles—from gritty neo‑noir to high‑stakes heist thrillers—and have been celebrated by critics, audiences, and genre communities alike.

| # | Film | Director | Notable Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern psychological thriller that blends horror with crime‑thriller elements. Moss delivers a powerhouse performance as a woman hunted by an unseen stalker, while the film’s tight pacing and inventive use of technology keep viewers on edge. |
| 2 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Michelle Dockery | Ritchie’s signature fast‑paced, witty style shines in this British gangster caper. The ensemble cast, snappy dialogue, and intricate plot twists make it a standout in the crime‑thriller arena. |
| 3 | **The Night Clerk** | Daniel Kwan | John Krasinski, Olivia Cooke | A tense, atmospheric thriller about a hotel clerk who becomes entangled in a murder investigation. The film’s moody cinematography and strong character work create a palpable sense of dread. |
| 4 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | Though more of a social thriller, its exploration of paranoia, betrayal, and moral ambiguity fits well within the crime‑thriller spectrum. The film’s stark realism and powerful performances earn it critical acclaim. |
| 5 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A historical crime‑thriller that reimagines the last legally sanctioned duel in France. Scott’s meticulous production design, combined with stellar acting and a gripping narrative, earned the film an Oscar nomination for Best Picture. |
| 6 | **The Devil All the Time** | Antonio Campos | Tom Holland, Robert Pattinson, Riley Keough | A bleak, atmospheric crime‑drama that follows a series of murders across rural America. Its haunting score, strong ensemble cast, and unsettling tone make it a memorable entry in the genre. |
| 7 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | While primarily a courtroom drama, its depiction of political intrigue, conspiracy, and civil unrest gives it a crime‑thriller edge. Sorkin’s razor‑sharp dialogue and the film’s timely subject matter earned it an Oscar nomination for Best Picture. |
| 8 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | A sprawling crime epic that spans decades, exploring the lives of mob hitmen and their relationships. Scorsese’s masterful storytelling, combined with De Niro, Pacino, and Pesci’s iconic performances, earned the film an Oscar nomination for Best Picture. |

Scorsese’s masterful storytelling, combined with De Niro, Pacino, and Pesci’s iconic performances, earned the film an Oscar nomination for Best Picture. |

Scorsese’s masterful storytelling, combined with De Niro, Pacino, and Pesci’s iconic performances, earned the film an Oscar nomination for Best Picture. |
